# 040 · Nest-based private access (JEP 181), reviewed as four lines of a 120-line contract

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✓ Verified: all 120 cases match** | functional, no-false-positive | none | feature, behaviour change intended | [`AccessControl#check`](../../examples/apps/mica/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/mica/link/AccessControl.java) | [B8: Behavioural contracts](../../lib/README.md) |

> Access control admits a `private` member from its declaring class only; nestmates reach each other through the synthetic accessors javac generates. A developer implements JEP 181: a `private` member is also accessible from a class in the same nest. The behavioural contract is regenerated, and its diff is the four cases where the visibility is `private` and the relation is `same nest`, each `false` to `true`. The other 116 cases are proved unchanged, and the diff is what the reviewer approves.

Tags: [access-control](../README.md#tag-access-control), [jvm-internals](../README.md#tag-jvm-internals), [contract-diff-review](../README.md#tag-contract-diff-review)

## The change

For a `private` member, answer `true` when the relation is `SAME_CLASS` or `SAME_NEST`: a class and its nestmates (`NestHost` and `NestMembers`, class file version 55) share their private members, so javac no longer has to generate accessors for inner classes. The test for private access gains the nestmate case, and the contract is regenerated.

**Before** ([`AccessControl.java`](../../examples/apps/mica/src/main/java/net/terminalvalue/mica/link/AccessControl.java), line 19):

```java
public static boolean check(Visibility member, Relation relation, boolean staticMember, boolean objectrefIsCurrentOrSubclass) {
    return switch (member) {
        case PUBLIC -> true;
        // Nest-based access control (JEP 181) is not implemented yet: nestmates reach each other's private
        // members through the synthetic accessors javac generates for class files before version 55.
        case PRIVATE -> relation == Relation.SAME_CLASS;
        case PACKAGE_PRIVATE -> relation == Relation.SAME_CLASS || relation == Relation.SAME_NEST || relation == Relation.SAME_PACKAGE;
        case PROTECTED -> switch (relation) {
            case SAME_CLASS, SAME_NEST, SAME_PACKAGE -> true;
```

**After:**

```java
public static boolean check(Visibility member, Relation relation, boolean staticMember, boolean objectrefIsCurrentOrSubclass) {
    return switch (member) {
        case PUBLIC -> true;
        // Nest-based access control (JEP 181): a class and its nestmates share their private members, so that
        // javac need not generate synthetic accessors for inner classes.
        case PRIVATE -> relation == Relation.SAME_CLASS || relation == Relation.SAME_NEST;
        case PACKAGE_PRIVATE -> relation == Relation.SAME_CLASS || relation == Relation.SAME_NEST || relation == Relation.SAME_PACKAGE;
        case PROTECTED -> switch (relation) {
            case SAME_CLASS, SAME_NEST, SAME_PACKAGE -> true;
```

All 120 possible inputs give the same outcome as the contract.

Because the change was intended, the developer regenerated the contract. This diff is what the reviewer approves:

@@ -80,10 +80,10 @@

+check(PRIVATE, SAME_NEST, true, false)                          => true
+check(PRIVATE, SAME_NEST, true, true)                           => true
 check(PRIVATE, SAME_PACKAGE, false, false)                      => false

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

Every existing unit test passes, as it should (`java -ea net.terminalvalue.mica.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

The intended change is four cases; the risk is a fifth. The private rule sits in a `switch` next to the package and protected rules, and a nest relation that leaks into either of those (a nestmate in another package, which cannot exist but which the enum does not forbid; a protected rule that starts treating nestmates as subclasses) would be a change to access control nobody asked for. A reviewer reading the Java sees one line change and takes the author's word for its scope; the contract diff shows the scope.

## Why the verdict is right

Because the change is intended, the generator regenerates the contract from the patched bytecode before verifying, and records the diff. The diff has four lines, `check(PRIVATE, SAME_NEST, s, o)` for the four combinations of the two booleans, each `false` to `true`; no other case moved. The verifier then proves the patched bytecode pure and runs all 120 cases against the regenerated contract, which pass. The four lines are the specification of JEP 181 at the level of this kernel: private members are shared within a nest and nowhere else, whatever the member's staticness or the receiver.

## What to do

Merge, with the contract diff as the review record. The next change to access control is checked against these 120 cases, nestmates included.

## Evidence

The proof trusted these JDK APIs to be pure: `java.lang.Enum.ordinal`, `java.lang.MatchException.<init>`, `java.lang.Record.<init>`, `java.lang.runtime.SwitchBootstraps.typeSwitch`, `java.util.List.copyOf`, `java.util.List.of`, `java.util.Objects.requireNonNull`.
